title: Gypsophila: A Scalable and Bandwidth-Optimized Multi-Scalar Multiplication Architecture
problem: Multi-Scalar Multiplication (MSM) is computationally intensive and bandwidth-constrained, particularly in Zero-knowledge proof systems. Scaling MSM to multiple processing elements results in high area overhead and bandwidth pressure.
motivation: MSM is a fundamental cryptographic primitive crucial for Zero-knowledge proof systems, requiring efficient hardware acceleration for practical deployment.
method: The paper optimizes single MSM Process Elements using bucket methods with fewer conflicts enhanced by greedy-based scheduling. Gypsophila scales this to multiple PEs by balancing dataflow through bucket classification, bucket aggregation, and result aggregation stages. Multiple PEs with different access patterns share a universal point input channel and post-processing unit to reduce resource duplication and bandwidth contention.
key_novelty: Shared input channel and post-processing unit architecture enabling multiple independent MSM processing elements to operate with significantly reduced bandwidth and area overhead while maintaining near-linear scalability.
contributions: Optimized single MSM PE achieving 2x average speedup (3.63x peak) over prior implementations
Gypsophila scalable multi-PE architecture with shared resource infrastructure
Balanced dataflow design reducing bandwidth to 1/16 of non-optimized 16-PE baseline
16 PEs completing 16 MSM tasks in 1.01% additional time with 7.8% area savings

metrics.speedup: 2x average (3.63x peak) single PE; 16x with 16 PEs in 1.01% additional time

primary_theme: Scalable cryptographic accelerator with shared resource optimization
